hotel.how.title: How to Make a Hotel Lobby AI Video
hotel.how.one.title: Pick two clear portraits
hotel.how.one.text: Choose one clear photo for each performer. A visible face, natural expression and similar camera angle give the video model a stronger reference for keeping two people distinct.
hotel.how.two.title: Set the timing
hotel.how.two.text: Write a simple sequence: person A begins, person B reacts, then the lead changes. A fixed camera and small gestures usually make the first attempt easier to judge.
hotel.how.three.title: Generate and review
hotel.how.three.text: Press generate, choose a plan, and we compose both people in the orange booth before transferring the Hotel Lobby performance and audio onto them. Review identity, hands, the center microphone and left-right placement before you share.
hotel.ideas.title: Hotel Lobby AI Ideas for Friends, Siblings and Couples
hotel.ideas.description: The duet works best when the relationship between the two performers is easy to understand. Start with one moment, one camera angle and a clear handoff.
hotel.ideas.friends.title: Friends on the mic
hotel.ideas.friends.text: Make a call and response: one friend takes the first line, the other answers at the mic. Use eye contact, smiles and small gestures to show their connection.
hotel.ideas.siblings.title: Sibling back and forth
hotel.ideas.siblings.text: One sibling starts confidently; the other joins on the next beat. Keep them on opposite sides of the orange booth and let their expressions tell the story.
hotel.ideas.couples.title: Couples in sync
hotel.ideas.couples.text: Give a couple a quiet first verse and a shared chorus. Keep the gestures small and let a glance across the microphone mark the moment they come together.
hotel.bottom.title: The mic is waiting.
hotel.bottom.text: Choose your two performers and make the lobby scene your own.
hotel.footer.line: Create a two-person AI duet video with Hotel Lobby AI.

hotel.explainer.title: What is the Hotel Lobby AI filter?
hotel.explainer.origin: The trend comes from a real performance. On June 17, 2022, the COLORS YouTube channel released Quavo and Takeoff performing their song "Hotel Lobby" against a flat orange backdrop, trading lines on a single microphone hung from the ceiling. In September 2026 creators on TikTok and X began using AI video tools to swap the two rappers for friends, couples, celebrities, fictional characters and even pets while keeping the original moves, lip-sync and audio — and the "Hotel Lobby AI" meme took off.
hotel.explainer.one: Two subjects stand on opposite sides of one hanging microphone while the camera holds steady. One leads, the other reacts, and then they trade the moment. Friends, partners or family members can appear together even when their source photos were taken separately.
hotel.explainer.two: This page makes that look for you. Choose two portraits, decide who appears on each side and optionally add a styling note. We compose the scene with GPT Image 2 and animate it with DreamActor motion transfer, which carries over the reference performance and its audio.
hotel.explainer.three: Think of it as a short scene. A good result keeps each person recognizable, gives both people room and places the microphone between them. Orange walls, warm light and a steady camera unify the setup. Results vary with the model and photos, so review the clip before posting.
hotel.guide.title: Make your Hotel Lobby AI duet look more like your people
hotel.guide.intro: A precise prompt helps, but the photos you choose set the ceiling for the final scene. These checks can reduce common identity and composition problems before you generate.
hotel.guide.photos.title: Start with useful portraits
hotel.guide.photos.text: Use sharp images with full faces and enough clothing to guide the scene. Avoid heavy filters, sunglasses, crowded backgrounds and cropped faces. Similar lighting and perspective can make the duet feel more consistent. If one portrait is a close-up and the other shows a full body, crop or replace one so the references match more closely. Neutral expressions leave more room for a believable reaction. Only transform images you have permission to use.
hotel.guide.motion.title: Keep the action readable
hotel.guide.motion.text: Describe one short exchange: a lead singer, a listening reaction and a handoff. Ask for natural mouth movement and small gestures while the camera stays centered. State whose lips move in each beat so the performers do not appear to sing the same line at once. Fast turns and sudden cuts can make faces or left-right positions harder to preserve.
hotel.guide.review.title: Inspect the first take
hotel.guide.review.text: Watch the clip before sharing. Confirm that A stays left, B stays right and the microphone stays between them. Check for warped hands, merged faces, extra people or changing outfits. Watch once with the sound off: the handoff should still make visual sense. If a face changes midway, shorten the scene before adding more movement. If the scene breaks, simplify your direction and try again.
hotel.prompt.title: Hotel Lobby AI Prompt (Copy and Paste)
hotel.prompt.one: For a Hotel Lobby AI duet, the starter prompt names the main visual anchors: a vertical 9:16 frame, a matte-orange booth, two separate people, one black microphone, soft light and a locked camera. It also asks the model to preserve faces and outfits and avoid side swaps, added people, captions and watermarks. These constraints give the generator a clearer shot list than a vague request to make two photos sing together.
hotel.prompt.two: Use the direction field for one styling detail, such as outfits, accessories or expressions. Keep it short so the core composition still leads — the booth, the center microphone and left-right placement are fixed by the base prompt. If the first result is off, change one thing at a time and generate again.
hotel.prompt.copy_text: Two people from my two reference photos perform a duet in a seamless burnt-orange recording booth. Person A (photo 1) stands on the left, Person B (photo 2) on the right, facing each other across one black microphone hanging at face level in the exact center. Vertical 9:16, static centered camera, soft even studio light, framed from the knees up. A sings the first line while B listens and nods; B takes the next line while A reacts; then they share the mic. Natural lip-sync and small hand gestures. Keep each face, hairstyle and outfit unchanged. No side swaps, no extra people, no captions, no watermark.
hotel.faq.title: Hotel Lobby AI FAQ
hotel.faq.one.question: Can I generate the duet video on this page?
hotel.faq.one.answer: Yes. Sign in, upload one photo for each side and press Generate. The scene is ready in under a minute and the finished video in about 3–5 minutes. Each video uses credits.
hotel.faq.two.question: What happens to my photos?
hotel.faq.two.answer: When you press Generate, your two photos are resized in your browser and sent to our AI provider (fal.ai) to create the scene and the video. They are not uploaded before you press Generate. Only use photos you have permission to use.
hotel.faq.three.question: Can I make the duet with two separate photos?
hotel.faq.three.answer: Yes. Use one clear reference for each person, with A on the left and B on the right. Identity preservation depends on the generator and photos, so inspect the result.
hotel.faq.four.question: Why do the faces or positions change in my result?
hotel.faq.four.answer: Models can drift when references are unclear or actions are busy. Use visible faces, remove camera moves and describe a shorter exchange. Repeat left-right placement and request one continuous shot. A usable clip may take several tries.
hotel.faq.five.question: Can I use photos of a couple or friends?
hotel.faq.five.answer: Yes. The orange booth can frame a couple, friends or family — including a parent and their child, as long as you're that child's parent or legal guardian. Change the performance direction but keep identities separate. Get permission from everyone pictured and identify the result as AI-generated when you share it.
hotel.faq.six.question: How much does a Hotel Lobby AI video cost?
hotel.faq.six.answer: Every generation uses credits, and the exact amount is shown on the button and in the pricing section. Choose a one-time pack or subscribe monthly. If a generation fails, the credits go back to your balance automatically.
hotel.faq.seven.question: What is the hotel lobby AI trend?
hotel.faq.seven.answer: It is a two-person duet scene in an orange recording booth. One person starts a line beside a hanging microphone, and the other responds. Creators often use two separate photos to plan a shared AI video scene.
hotel.faq.eight.question: Is the video generated on this site?
hotel.faq.eight.answer: Yes. The scene preview and the finished video are both generated here on Hotel Lobby AI — you don't need any other app or account. Finished videos are saved in My videos.

admin.funnel.title: Funnel dashboard
admin.funnel.description: Unique-visitor conversion from the site's own event table. Days are cut at UTC+8.
admin.funnel.card.unpaid_hint: Users who reached a payment page in the last 24h and have not paid since.
admin.funnel.footnote.title: Definitions
admin.funnel.footnote.unique: Every step counts unique visitors (hl_did cookie), not impressions; percentages under each step are relative to visitors in the same row. The daily table de-duplicates within each UTC+8 day.
admin.funnel.footnote.visit: Visitors = browsers that opened the generator page (/ or /ai-livestream, event hl_home_view, sent from the browser; bot user agents dropped).
admin.funnel.footnote.first_touch: Source / country = external referrer or utm_source and cf-ipcountry at the visitor's first event, pinned by cookie. Visitors who came before tracking shipped are attributed to their first visit after it.
admin.funnel.footnote.checkout: Sent to payment = the server created a payment session (/api/payment/checkout); provider is the one actually used.
admin.funnel.footnote.paid: Payers / revenue come from the order table (status = paid, by paid_at), so webhook-only payments count. Source/country use the payer's earliest event, build uses their latest checkout; payers with no events show as unknown. Revenue sums order amounts with no currency conversion.
admin.funnel.footnote.provider: Provider table is by order creation time: payment success = orders paid ÷ orders created (abandoned checkouts count as unpaid).
admin.funnel.footnote.build: Build = git commit of the page/server that sent the event.
admin.funnel.footnote.compare: Today vs yesterday compares the same clock time: today 00:00 → now against yesterday 00:00 → this time yesterday (UTC+8).
admin.funnel.footnote.excluded: Excluded: test user {ids} and every visitor id that user has used.
admin.funnel.section.history: Traffic since launch (Cloudflare Web Analytics + orders)
admin.funnel.history.synced: Traffic imported through {day}. Run `npx tsx scripts/sync-traffic.ts` to refresh.
admin.funnel.history.not_synced: No traffic imported yet. Run `npx tsx scripts/sync-traffic.ts`.
admin.funnel.footnote.history: Traffic since launch: browser page views and visits come from Cloudflare Web Analytics (a JS beacon only real browsers send, so crawlers are excluded) imported by scripts/sync-traffic.ts. It is sampled: page views are the steadier number; visits (page loads arriving from outside the site) are a rough estimate at this traffic level, so no conversion rate is computed from them. Free previews = distinct devices (the feature ran Oct 2–9). Sign-ups, started checkout (distinct users who created an order), payers and revenue come from the user and order tables. The CN/HK switch only removes those countries from page views and visits.
admin.funnel.footnote.history_referrer: Referrers come from the browser's Referer header. ChatGPT strips it, so most ChatGPT clicks show as direct here; the user table's utm_source (chatgpt.com) is the reliable ChatGPT signal. /admin pages are excluded from traffic and the top pages list.

dc.faq.title: DeckCraft *questions*, answered.
dc.faq.body: Straight answers before your first slide.
dc.faq.free.a: Yes. The ArtCraft team publishes DeckCraft as open-source software under MIT or Apache-2.0 licensing. You can use the desktop and web builds without buying a subscription.
dc.faq.pptx.q: Can I open my PowerPoint files?
dc.faq.pptx.a: DeckCraft can open and save .pptx presentations. It is still in early development, so complex formatting, media, or advanced PowerPoint features may not round-trip perfectly. Always work from a copy and check the exported result.
dc.faq.browser.q: How does the online editor work?
dc.faq.browser.a: Start the DeckCraft online editor directly on this page by choosing a blank presentation or a sample deck. It runs the actual open-source WebAssembly build, rather than a screenshot or demo animation. Open files from your device and save or export them back to it. A modern desktop browser with WebGPU or WebGL2 works best; the first launch downloads the app.
dc.faq.account.q: Do I need an account? Where are my files?
dc.faq.account.a: No account is required to try the editor or download the software. Documents are handled in the browser and saved to your device; this site does not provide cloud document storage or real-time collaboration. Save your work before closing the tab.
dc.faq.official.q: Is deckcraft.me the official DeckCraft website?
dc.faq.official.a: No. This is an independent English-language guide and browser access point. DeckCraft is developed by the ArtCraft team at Storytold. Official source, downloads, and project information are linked throughout this site.

dc.guide.step1.title: Create your first slide
dc.guide.step1.body: Start a new presentation or open a sample deck to explore. The ribbon holds your editing tools, thumbnails organize your slides, and the canvas is where your idea takes shape.
dc.guide.step1.a: Choose a slide layout with placeholders that suit your content.
dc.guide.step1.b: Add a title and a short supporting sentence. Keep one main idea on each slide.
dc.guide.step1.c: Use the slide thumbnails to select the slide you want to edit.
dc.guide.step1.alt: Official DeckCraft editor showing the ribbon, slide thumbnails, canvas and notes
dc.guide.step2.title: Make the words work
dc.guide.step2.body: Click into a text placeholder to edit in place. Select text to change its font, size, color and paragraph formatting. A clear hierarchy makes the story easier to follow.
dc.guide.step2.a: Use a large title and readable body text.
dc.guide.step2.b: Try bullets or numbering for short, structured ideas.
dc.guide.step2.c: Explore the format pane for more detailed styling controls.
dc.guide.step2.alt: Official DeckCraft format pane showing gradient and shape styling controls
dc.guide.step3.title: Give your ideas a shape
dc.guide.step3.body: Add shapes, pictures, tables or charts to explain what words alone cannot. Selecting an object reveals the relevant formatting tools.
dc.guide.step3.a: Insert a shape, then drag its handles to change its size.
dc.guide.step3.b: Use fills, outlines and alignment to make a consistent visual language.
dc.guide.step3.c: Add pictures and crop them to focus on the part that matters.
dc.guide.step3.alt: Official DeckCraft Shape Format tab and a selected shape with adjustment handles
dc.guide.step4.title: Bring the story to life
dc.guide.step4.body: Use Slide Sorter to review the flow of your deck. Add transitions between slides, then try the full-screen slide show to see the story as your audience will.
dc.guide.step4.a: Review slide order before adding transitions.
dc.guide.step4.b: Use transitions and animations sparingly to guide attention.
dc.guide.step4.c: Rehearse the slide show and check media playback before presenting.
dc.guide.step4.alt: Official DeckCraft Slide Sorter with transitions displayed below slides
dc.guide.step5.title: Save, share, and keep creating
dc.guide.step5.body: Save your work regularly. DeckCraft supports opening and saving .pptx presentations, plus PDF and image export. The app is still in alpha, so review the result in its destination app.
dc.guide.step5.a: Keep an original copy before importing an important presentation.
dc.guide.step5.b: Export a PDF when you want a fixed layout for reading or sharing.
dc.guide.step5.c: Check fonts, charts, transitions and media after exchanging .pptx files.
dc.guide.step5.alt: Official DeckCraft in dark mode with a chart on the slide canvas

dc.about.title: What is *DeckCraft*?
dc.about.p1: DeckCraft is free, open-source presentation software for making slides, building decks, and presenting them. It is developed by the ArtCraft team at Storytold, written in pure Rust, and released under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license. Run it as a native desktop app on macOS, Windows, and Linux, or open the same editor in your browser through WebAssembly with nothing to install.
dc.about.p2: The DeckCraft online editor puts slide thumbnails on the left, a canvas in the middle, and formatting tools within reach. If you know PowerPoint, Keynote, or Google Slides, the workspace should feel familiar. Start with a sample presentation on this page, or create a blank deck and build your own story. The source code is open to read, build, and improve, with no subscription required.
dc.about.slides.title: DeckCraft slides: what you can build
dc.about.slides.body: DeckCraft slides cover the everyday work of a presentation. Start from a theme, set up slide masters and reusable layouts, then add text, pictures, charts, and vector shapes. Group the deck into sections, write speaker notes, and style shapes with fills, gradients, and outlines. When the content is ready, add transitions plus entrance, emphasis, and exit animations to tell the story one point at a time.
dc.about.pptx.title: Edit PowerPoint files with DeckCraft
dc.about.pptx.body: DeckCraft opens and saves .pptx, the format Microsoft PowerPoint uses, so you can take a deck a colleague sent, edit it, and send it back. The project is still in early development, so complex formatting, embedded media, and advanced PowerPoint features may not round-trip perfectly. Work from a copy of important files and check the result before you share it.
dc.about.online.title: DeckCraft online editor and desktop app
dc.about.online.body: Use the DeckCraft online editor on this page without an account or installer. The browser runs the real open-source WebAssembly build, with WebGPU or WebGL2 support. Open presentations from your device and save your work before leaving. For longer editing sessions, the DeckCraft desktop app offers a universal Mac build, Windows installers and portable downloads, plus AppImage, .deb, and .rpm packages for Linux.
dc.about.who.title: Who DeckCraft is for
dc.about.who.body: Use DeckCraft slides for class projects, teaching materials, project updates, and talks. Students can build a presentation without buying another subscription. Teachers can prepare lesson slides on a school laptop. Linux users can choose a native app, while developers can inspect the source. Try your own workflow with a small deck first, especially when exchanging files with PowerPoint users.

dc.howto.present.body: Go full screen, follow your speaker notes, and rehearse your timing. Save back to .pptx when you are done.

dc.faq.make.q: What can I make with DeckCraft slides?
dc.faq.make.a: Pitch decks, class presentations, lesson slides, project updates, and conference talks. DeckCraft covers themes, layouts, text, images, charts, shapes, transitions, animations, and speaker notes, which is what most everyday presentations need.
dc.faq.platforms.q: Does DeckCraft work on Mac, Windows, and Linux?
dc.faq.platforms.a: Yes. DeckCraft ships a universal macOS build for Apple silicon and Intel, Windows installers for x64 and ARM64 plus a portable zip, and Linux packages as AppImage, .deb, and .rpm. The online editor covers other systems with a modern desktop browser.
dc.faq.alternative.q: Is DeckCraft a good PowerPoint alternative?
dc.faq.alternative.a: For everyday decks, yes, especially if you want free, open-source software or a native Linux app. PowerPoint still leads on advanced features, add-ins, and real-time co-authoring. Our DeckCraft vs. PowerPoint page walks through the differences honestly.
